GREENVILLE, S.C., October 28, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Regional Management Corp. (NYSE: RM), a diversified consumer finance company, announced today the appointment of Elizabeth Canini as Chief Credit Risk Officer, effective November 2, 2026.

Ms. Canini has more than 25 years of credit risk and consumer lending experience, with senior leadership roles at Citi, PNC, and HSBC. Most recently, she served as Managing Director and Senior Credit Officer for the Retail Bank at Citi, where she held independent second-line credit authority over the bank's global residential mortgage portfolio. Prior to Citi, she spent 11 years at PNC, most recently as Senior Vice President and Head of Product Management – Student and Personal Lending, where she held full P&L responsibility for the bank's unsecured personal lending and student lending portfolios. She began her career at HSBC, where she spent more than a decade in various credit risk roles.

"We are pleased to welcome Liz to Regional," said Lakhbir S. Lamba, President and Chief Executive Officer of Regional Management Corp. "Liz has led consumer lending businesses and successfully overseen the credit management of large, complex portfolios, which gives her a balanced view of both growth and risk. Her depth in credit policy, analytics, and portfolio management will serve Regional well as we continue to focus on driving sustainable and profitable growth. In addition, I want to thank Manish Parmar for his many contributions to Regional over the past six years."

"Regional has built a strong franchise serving customers who rely on accessible, easy-to-understand financial solutions," said Ms. Canini. "I look forward to working with Lakhbir and the Regional team to further strengthen our credit capabilities and support responsible growth."

About Regional Management Corp.

Regional Management Corp. (NYSE: RM) is a diversified consumer finance company that provides attractive, easy-to-understand installment loan products primarily to customers with limited access to consumer credit from banks, thrifts, credit card companies, and other lenders. Regional Management operates under the name "Regional Finance" online and in branch locations in 20 states across the United States. Each of its loan products is structured on a fixed-rate, fixed-term basis with fully amortizing equal monthly installment payments, repayable at any time without penalty. Regional Management sources loans through its multiple channel platform, which includes branches, centrally managed direct mail campaigns, digital partners, and its consumer website. For more information, please visit www.RegionalManagement.com.

title: FLG Cuts NII & EPS Outlook, Pushes 2027 Profitability Target to 2028
detail:
FLG Cuts NII & EPS Outlook, Pushes 2027 Profitability Target to 2028

Trading disclosure

During its third-quarter 2026 earnings conference call, Flagstar Bank, National Association FLG lowered its net interest income (NII) and adjusted earnings per share (EPS) outlook for 2026 and 2027. The downward revisions reflect higher anticipated credit costs, competitive deposit pricing and slower balance-sheet growth, pushing FLG's 2027 profitability targets to 2028.

Flagstar now expects NII of $1.82-$1.83 billion for 2026, down from its previous forecast of $1.86-$1.96 billion. The bank also slashed its adjusted EPS guidance to 10-15 cents from 40-50 cents of prior guidance. The revised outlook reflects higher anticipated credit provisions and slower balance-sheet growth amid a challenging interest rate environment.

Looking ahead to 2027, the bank projects NII of $2.20-$2.30 billion compared with its earlier guidance of $2.50-$2.65 billion. Meanwhile, its adjusted EPS is now expected to be 85-95 cents, substantially below the previous projection of $1.60-$1.70.

The weaker outlook largely reflects expectations of sustained higher interest rates, intensifying deposit competition and slower balance-sheet growth. In September 2026, the Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points, with management expecting three additional hikes through June 2027. Slower deposit growth is expected to limit commercial and industrial (C&I) loan growth, while weaker mortgage originations and delayed resolution of nonaccrual loans will continue to weigh on NII. Additionally, rising credit risks, particularly in the New York City rent-regulated multifamily portfolio, prompted management to raise its provision for loan losses outlook to $160-$170 million for 2026 from $90-$140 million and to $175-$225 million for 2027 from $100-$150 million.

Due to near-term challenges, Flagstar has pushed its earlier 2027 profitability targets to 2028, projecting NII of $2.60-$2.70 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.60-$1.70 for the year. Repricing low-yielding loans, growth in higher-yielding C&I lending and an improving funding mix are expected to support earnings recovery. However, elevated credit costs and slower deposit growth remain key risks to achieving these targets.

2026 Outlook of FLG Peers

Similar to FLG, Huntington Bancshares Incorporated HBAN and Citigroup Inc. C have revised their outlooks.

At the Barclays 24th Annual Global Financial Services Conference, Huntington Bancshares lowered its 2026 net interest income growth outlook to approximately 35% from its previous projection of 39-43%, based on the 2025 baseline of $6.06 billion. Higher deposit costs, pricing competition and weaker loan volumes are likely to limit Huntington Bancshares' net interest margin expansion.

Citigroup Inc. C continues to demonstrate meaningful improvement in profitability, supported by robust revenue growth, operating efficiency gains and disciplined execution of its transformation initiatives. In the first nine months of 2026, return on tangible common equity (RoTCE) improved 400 basis points (bps) year over year to 12.6%, underscoring the company's strengthening earnings-generating capabilities and progress toward achieving sustainable returns.

The profitability improvement was driven by broad-based growth across Citigroup's core businesses. Meanwhile, operating expenses increased a modest 3% to $42.48 billion, significantly below the pace of revenue growth. Consequently, the efficiency ratio improved to 58% from 63.2% in the year-ago period, highlighting positive operating leverage and improving cost efficiency.

Looking ahead, Citigroup's diversified revenue streams, ongoing business simplification and disciplined capital allocation are expected to support profitability. Management anticipates 2026 RoTCE above 11%, while targeting 11-13% for 2027-2028. Continued expansion in fee-generating businesses, improving operating leverage and shareholder-friendly capital distributions could further strengthen its earnings outlook. However, elevated credit costs, transformation-related expenses and macroeconomic uncertainty remain the key challenges.

Against this backdrop, should investors continue holding on to the C stock to capitalize on its improving fundamentals? Let us delve deeper to answer this.

Citigroup's Performance Catalysts

Strategic Streamlining Efforts: Citigroup has moved closer to completing its multi-year exit from non-core international consumer banking. The sale of the Polish consumer business in June 2026 marked the final international consumer divestiture apart from remaining wind-downs of Banamex. The company also sold an additional 22.6% stake in Banamex in the second quarter after selling 25% in late 2025. The remaining Banamex deconsolidation and IPO are planned for early 2027, with management expecting the transaction to free up $5 billion in capital.

These transactions follow the completed Russia exit and divestitures of consumer franchises across Asia and EMEA. The simpler structure reduces operational complexity, releases capital and allows management to direct resources toward Services, Markets, Banking, Wealth and U.S. Consumer Cards. During the second-quarter earnings call, management highlighted continued investment in U.S. Consumer Cards, including product development, partnerships and customer acquisition.

Bank of America BAC has sustained robust net interest income (NII) growth so far this year, driven by healthy loan and deposit expansion, fixed-rate asset repricing and higher contributions from Global Markets activities. The banking giant's improving NII trajectory underscores its balance-sheet strength and ability to navigate a shifting rate environment.

After rising 7.1% year over year to $15.75 billion in the first quarter, BAC's NII increased 9% to $16 billion in the second quarter. The momentum extended into the third quarter, with NII advancing 8% to a record $16.45 billion. The net interest yield expanded 15 basis points year over year to 2.16% in the third quarter, while ending loans and leases grew 7% to $1.25 trillion, reinforcing the bank's interest-earning capacity.

Looking ahead, BAC remains optimistic about sustaining the NII momentum, with management projecting NII growth of 8% in 2026 and at least 8% in 2027. Continued balance-sheet expansion and favorable fixed-rate asset repricing are expected to underpin this growth, providing a tailwind to profitability despite interest-rate uncertainties.

With NII momentum strengthening and a favorable growth outlook, does BAC present a compelling investment opportunity at the current levels? While improving interest income strengthens the investment case, an assessment of the bank's other fundamental strengths, potential headwinds and valuation is essential before making any investment decision.

BAC's Other Key Positives to Note:

Accelerating Digital & AI-Led Transformation: Bank of America continues to invest in digital banking, artificial intelligence (AI), payments infrastructure and branch expansion to strengthen customer engagement and operating efficiency. The bank plans to open at least 20 additional financial centers by year-end, following 14 openings in the third quarter.

The growing adoption of its AI-powered virtual assistant Erica and Zelle, alongside generative AI integration, is expected to enhance productivity and lower servicing costs. Meanwhile, investments in Swift and CashPro are strengthening its global payments capabilities, while the proposed Jio Credit investment offers exposure to India's expanding digital lending market.

Management expects benefits from its AI initiatives to rise from $250-$300 million in 2026 to $700 million in 2027. These investments should drive efficiency gains, diversify revenue opportunities and support long-term earnings growth.

Industry-Leading Deposit Franchise: Bank of America continues to benefit from its extensive, low-cost deposit franchise, providing a competitive advantage and a stable funding base. As of Sept. 30, 2026, loans and leases grew 7% year over year to $1.25 trillion, while deposits rose 1.8% to $2.04 trillion. Non-interest-bearing deposits contributed more than 75% to third-quarter deposit growth, with the average deposit rate remaining low at 1.49%.

BAC's diversified deposit base and favorable loan-to-deposit ratio provide flexibility to fund lending growth while limiting reliance on costly wholesale funding. These strengths, coupled with disciplined deposit pricing, should support NII growth, margins and profitability.

Robust Investment Banking (IB) Franchise: Bank of America's IB franchise continues to benefit from improving capital markets activity and a healthy deal pipeline. Following declines of 45.7% in 2022 and 2.4% in 2023, IB fees rebounded and grew 31.4% in 2024 and another 8.4% in 2025. The recovery continued in the first nine months of 2026, with IB fees rising 14.6% year over year.

While the company's third-quarter 2026 IB fees (excluding self-led deals) declined 11% year over year (reflecting softer advisory and debt underwriting activity), management remains optimistic about its robust deal pipeline. It continues to invest in bankers, technology and AI capabilities to strengthen execution and client engagement.

Looking ahead, a potential recovery in mergers and acquisitions (M&A), improving corporate confidence and stronger capital-raising activity should support fee income growth and earnings diversification, although elevated interest rates and geopolitical uncertainties remain near-term headwinds.

Robust Capital Returns Strategy: Bank of America continues to demonstrate its commitment to enhancing shareholder returns through consistent dividend growth and share repurchases. Following its successful performance in the 2026 Federal Reserve stress test, the bank increased its quarterly dividend 14.3% to 32 cents per share, marking its sixth consecutive annual dividend hike.

The company maintains an active capital return program, distributing $8.3 billion to shareholders in the third quarter of 2026, including $6 billion through share repurchases and $2.2 billion in common stock dividends.

Its common equity tier 1 (CET1) ratio stood at 10.9% as of Sept. 30, 2026, remaining above regulatory requirements. Supported by strong capital ratios, resilient earnings and excess capital generation, Bank of America remains well-positioned to sustain attractive shareholder distributions while supporting business growth.

Survey Finds 90% Of Large Businesses Are Embracing Tokenized Money

A new survey claims that nearly 90% of large businesses are using or testing tokenized money to improve cash management and cross-border payments.

The survey by Singapore-based bank DBS Group (SGX: D05) found that 88% of respondents reported live deployments or pilot tests involving tokenized cash.

The report found 24% had deployed the technology at scale, while 43% had limited live use in select markets.

Another 21% of large companies are running pilot programs, or proofs of concept, leaving 12% exploring the technology or not using it at all.

The survey polled 422 business across 11 markets, including the U.S., China, Germany, and the United Kingdom.

All the organizations polled had annual revenues of more than $500 million U.S.

Stablecoins led the instruments respondents are using or planning to adopt, at 63%, followed by tokenized deposits at 53% and tokenized money market funds at 52%.

Tokenized money is a digital representation of fiat currency issued on a blockchain or distributed ledger.

Benefits of tokenized money, according to advocates, are the ability to move money with greater speed and transparency.

About 70% of respondents said they already experienced improvements in real-time cross-border payments or expected them within two years using tokenized cash.

Regulatory uncertainty, security risks and integration difficulties remain obstacles to more widespread adoption of digital money, said DBS in its report.

Still, use of tokenized cash is growing quickly. U.S. bank Citigroup (NYSE: $C) said this spring that hundreds of clients were moving close to $1 billion U.S. daily through its Citi Token Service.

In September, DBS and Citigroup completed a weekend dollar payment between Singapore and New York using tokenized deposits through the Swift Digital Ledger.

DBS said the transaction settled within minutes and allowed funds to move outside traditional banking hours.

HSBC gets RBC target cut as Citi flags Hong Kong deposit risks Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

HSBC Holdings PLC (LSE:HSBA, NYSE:HSBC) price target was cut by RBC following lower profit forecasts, while Citi retained its 'neutral' rating amid questions over Hong Kong deposit migration.

RBC lowered its target to 1,325 pence from 1,375 pence and retained its sector perform' rating following the third-quarter results.

The broker cut its 2027 adjusted pre-tax profit estimate by 6% to $41.875 billion from $44.618 billion, mainly due to weaker net interest income from Hong Kong banking.

Its revised 2027 banking net interest income forecast of $48.3 billion includes contributions from asset growth, structural hedging and interest rates.

Offsetting some of those gains, RBC estimated that Hong Kong deposit migration and strategic exits would each subtract $0.6 billion from its income bridge.

The deposit outlook also featured in Citi's analysis, which examined the potential impact of further migration on interest income.

Citi said time deposits rose from 36% to 38% of HSBC's Hong Kong deposits, nearing the previous peak of 40% but still below the banking system average of 57%.

Against that backdrop, Citi questioned whether further migration explained HSBC's unchanged financial year 2026 net interest income guidance of more than $46 billion.

The broker noted that this guidance implied fourth-quarter income above $11.4 billion, compared with $11.7 billion in the third quarter, potentially signalling a lower exit trajectory into 2027.

Citi reported a 6% share-price fall despite small revenue misses and pre-tax profit in line with expectations, while RBC separately quoted a prior closing price of 1,291.40p.
